A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same GGM research work, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A-J. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of equations, tables, figures, and appendix material.

before.justification: v2 reports original GGM language-generation perplexities, image-generation FID scores, and conditional and unconditional generation examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original GGM experimental results in Tables 1-2 and the graphical and appendix generation examples.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, line 6 changes both log terms to negative terms, correcting the written loss to match Section 3.3's stated cross-entropy minimization. The architecture and sampling procedures remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change or retraining.

E1.justification: Both versions retain OpenWebText language generation, CelebA-HQ and FFHQ image generation, and the same zero-shot text and image infilling scenarios, including Appendices C and J.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same GPT2, BERT-large Gibbs sampling, Plaid, SEDD-medium, and MDLM comparators. Table 2 also retains the same image-generation comparator membership for each dataset.

E3.justification: Evaluation models, sampling settings, training budgets, and metric procedures remain unchanged, including 1,024 text generations and 50,000 images for FID. Although Algorithm 1 removes a multiple-timestep comment, Appendix H.1 still specifies 32 timesteps per language example.

E4.justification: The sampling-step comparison in Figure 2a, nearest-neighbor analysis in Appendix D, and conditional-generation case studies are unchanged. No ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point estimates without reported independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All tabulated results, plotted findings, and generation examples are unchanged. GGM's Table 1 perplexities remain 19.5, 19.9, and 18.0; Table 2 FIDs remain 9.8 on CelebA-HQ and 12.5 on FFHQ.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 corrects the formal definition of D_t,a to condition on the selected token being a, replacing the erroneous condition equating the remaining-token vector to a. Equation 3 also consistently uses the timestep-specific index. The existing proofs in Appendices A-B are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and discussion retain the same claims about reduction to binary classification, language and image generation performance, and zero-shot infilling capabilities.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning specialized tokenizers and potential performance improvements are unchanged. Both versions retain the same acknowledged performance gaps and Appendix I.2's caveats about FID and baseline preprocessing comparability.

D1.justification: Implementation, hardware, hyperparameter, tokenizer, training-time, and resource-access information remain unchanged. The deleted Algorithm 1 comment loses no unique implementation information because Appendix H.1 retains the explicit multiple-timestep setting.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, reference list, and positioning against variational discrete diffusion and ratio-matching approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes a few punctuation corrections, removes a redundant Algorithm 1 comment, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Section ordering, narrative structure, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-8 and Tables 1-2 retain their content, captions, structure, and placement. The localized textual and equation corrections cause only incidental reflow; there is no figure, table, or page-layout redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the loss signs in Algorithm 1 and the conditioning event in Section 3.3, making the formal training specification more internally consistent and easier to implement faithfully. These corrections improve technical accuracy while the empirical evidence, claims, limitations, and appendices remain unchanged.
